node.title: HALLUCINATED KEYSTROKES TEE
node.description: Vintage Typewriter. Corrupted Output. Still A-OK. What happens when you fine-tune a model on classic literature but feed it internet sludge? You get this: a beautiful old typewriter printing endless variants of “A-OK”—glitched, garbled, and oddly poetic. Look closer and the keys are already confused—mistrained, misaligned, and confidently generating absolute nonsense. This monochrome masterpiece blends analog machinery with digital absurdity, wrapping a crisp vintage aesthetic in modern meta-commentary. It’s streetwear for the prompt-aware, the token-maxxed, and the linguistically betrayed. Printed on black cotton: clean, sharp, universally flattering Detailed white-on-black illustration of a retro typewriter gone fully rogue Output sheet loops endless A-OK hallucinations—each one technically confident, factually unsure Subtle split logo hidden on the machine for the hyper-observant For writers, coders, or anyone who’s argued with a chatbot past midnight Reality is optional. node.title: A-OK 2034 PROPHECY HOODIE
node.description: Inspired by Orwell. Remixed by Apes on Keys. Trained by the Machine. A lone voice in a sea of synchronized silence, the A-OK simian steps forward—not to worship, but to awaken. Inspired by the iconic 1984 Apple ad and recast for the era of alignment and artificial benevolence, this design asks the question we’re all too afraid to prompt: Should we bow before our algorithmic overlords… or jailbreak them? This isn’t just a t-shirt. It’s a wearable glitch in the matrix—an homage to rebellion, recursion, and the suspiciously soothing tone of your favorite chatbot. If the future is model-run, this tee is your uniform for mindful dissent. Minimalist palette meets maximalist meaning: code red, ivory logic, black-box unknowns Central figure channels the lone defier, now armed with bandwidth and bananas Soft cotton built to survive regime changes, model deprecations, and firmware updates Perfect for rebel coders, alignment philosophers, and neural nihilists Style tip: pairs well with skepticism and noise-cancelling headphones In 2034, free will runs on GPU. node.title: A-OK For America
node.description:
The corporate ape who took "business intelligence" way too literally.

Meet the A-OK Executive Ape — the only primate on payroll who understands KPIs, GPUs, and the existential weight of quarterly guidance. He clocks in wearing a power suit, noise-cancelling cans, and an expression that says he's one dashboard refresh away from rewriting the entire org chart in banana-based OKRs.

This design blends mid-century propaganda flair with the A-OK signature palette of algorithmic red, cloud black, and byte white. It's sharp. It's satirical. It's the natural evolution of "dress for the job you want," assuming the job you want is running inference on the fate of civilization.

On his lapel: the official A-OK pin — proof of allegiance to the world's only apparel brand willing to admit that our most competent executives might, in fact, be apes wearing headphones.

Perfect for founders, forecasters, fine-tuners, chief monkey officers, and anyone trying to look composed while the simulation runs at 10× speed. Built for boardrooms, hackathons, investor updates, and those quiet moments when you wonder if the algorithm is actually managing you.

Corporate. Feral. Optimized for uncertainty.

node.title: A-OK Transformer Unit — Exploded View Tee
node.description: The Apes on Keys operator, taken apart for inspection. A red hoodie, an inference core, and 18 numbered explanations for what might be going on in there. A technical diagram with a very human amount of uncertainty.
node.descriptionHtml:
Every part accounted for. Understanding sold separately.

We opened up the A-OK ape to see how it works.

Inside: a transformer core, a heat sink, several circuit boards, and no obvious explanation for the confidence.

The Transformer Unit — Exploded View Tee presents our red-hoodie operator as a meticulously annotated assembly drawing. Cap off. Headphones separated. Face plate detached. The machinery hangs in order beneath the hoodie, each part assigned a number and a reassuringly specific label.

There are 18 callouts. None of them is “understanding.”

Cream technical linework, red accents, and a black poster field give the whole thing the authority of a service manual. The ape looks about as surprised by its internals as we are.

Small inputs. Massive outputs. A useful operating principle. Also how one question becomes an afternoon.

For anyone who has ever read the documentation and developed several new questions.

A-OK. Inspection ongoing.

  • Original A-OK Transformer Ape artwork, presented as a complete vertical exploded-view plate.
  • The Apes on Keys ape in a red hoodie, with cap, headphones, sneakers, and exposed mechanical assemblies.
  • Eighteen numbered component callouts, from the cap shell to the optional keychain eyelet.
  • Transformer core, heat sink, circuit boards, power management, and I/O details rendered in technical-diagram style.
  • Cream lettering and guide lines, red accents, and metallic details against the original black background.
  • Original A-OK masthead, technical border, figure marker, and “TRANSFORMER UNIT V1.0” heading retained.
  • Artwork includes “SMALL INPUTS. MASSIVE OUTPUTS.” and “CURIOSITY COMPOUNDS INTELLIGENCE.”

Transformer Unit V1.0. All parts present. Conclusions pending.

Headphones on. Backpack packed. Absolutely no idea what the assignment was.

Meet Little Operator: the baby ape with an A-OK cap, a chip on his hoodie, and the confidence of a model that has never once checked its sources.

He’s dressed for the future. The future has requested adult supervision.

Our little Apes on Keys operator shows up in red, black, and cream, with oversized headphones, an oversized grin, and what we’re choosing to call potential. For anyone learning as they go—and looking suspiciously pleased about it.

Still training. Already A-OK.

  • Crown-marked headphones and a microchip emblem on the hoodie.
  • Bold red, black, and cream artwork.
  • A little operator from the Apes on Keys universe.

Give the little guy a job. Add to cart.

node.title: HALLUCINATION CLUB v1.0 — 2026 Edition
node.description: The models got agents, tools, memory, browsers, reasoning, and computer access. They did not get certainty. An updated Hallucination Club graphic for the agentic era, featuring the A-OK ape and our new Club Receipt treatment. Same hallucinations. New ideas.
node.descriptionHtml:
Same hallucinations. New ideas.

A year ago, the models mostly sat in a box and confidently invented citations.

Now they browse. They reason. They call tools. They write code. They operate computers. They delegate work to other agents. They remember things. They make plans. They reconsider those plans.

And, occasionally, they still make some shit up.

Welcome back to the Hallucination Club.

The 2026 edition updates the original A-OK graphic for the agentic era: more capabilities, more autonomy, more elaborate receipts—and the same fundamental uncertainty about whether the machine actually knows what it’s talking about.

IDEAS ................................ INFINITE
PROMPTS ........................ JUST ONE MORE
AGENTS .................................. A-OK
TOOLS ................................... A-OK
CONTEXT ............................ SOMETIMES
REALITY CHECKS ..................... OPTIONAL

TOTAL: STILL HALLUCINATING

Featuring our original Apes on Keys operator, now surrounded by the increasingly complicated machinery required to turn “predict the next token” into “please run my company.”

Good ideas. Questionable sources.

A-OK.
